confidentiality: An unauthorised person may read private files.
integrity: They may change account details or coursework.
availability: They may lock the student out.
control: Use a long, unique passphrase and a password manager where permitted.
limitation: A strong password cannot prevent every phishing or device compromise.

asset: Student account and other accounts using the same password
confidentiality: A password exposed on one service may expose other accounts.
integrity: An intruder may alter information in reused-password accounts.
availability: Accounts may be locked or taken over.
control: Use a unique password for every account and change reused passwords.
limitation: Unique passwords do not protect against malware or deceptive sign-in pages.

confidentiality: An unexpected approval may allow an unauthorised sign-in.
integrity: An intruder may change account information.
control: Deny unexpected prompts and report repeated requests to IT.
limitation: MFA is an additional layer, not a guarantee against every attack.

asset: Laptop, operating system, and project files
confidentiality: Unpatched weaknesses may expose stored information.
availability: A device may become unstable or unavailable.
control: Install updates promptly through trusted system settings.
limitation: Updates reduce known risks but cannot eliminate all vulnerabilities.

risk: Friend uses laptop while student is signed in
asset: Signed-in student session and local project files
confidentiality: The friend may see private account information.
integrity: Files or settings may be changed accidentally or intentionally.
availability: Files may be moved or deleted.
control: Lock the screen when stepping away and use separate user accounts.
limitation: Physical access controls depend on consistent use and do not replace backups.
